me the timeline of AI virtual labs development.AI Mode reply for Give me the timeline of AI virtual labs development.The evolution of AI virtual labs—environments where AI agents autonomously hypothesize, simulate, and design experiments before (or instead of) physical deployment—has transitioned rapidly from basic software scripts to complex, multi-agent closed loops. Robot on RailsThe developmental timeline spans from early digital simulators to the highly autonomous, decentralized scientific frameworks dominating 2023–2026. Association of American Universities (AAU)Phase 1: Digital Replicas & Simulation (Pre-2018)Before AI acted as a primary thinker, virtual labs were essentially passive software tools meant for human training or data recording. 1990s–2010s: Development of interactive, screen-based physics and chemistry applications (e.g., standard circuit simulators or titration software). Niobium-Tin Magnets: Teams began dismantling and cutting the first magnet connections to remove 28 massive superconducting focusing magnets (the "inner triplets") located near the collision points. The original niobium-titanium magnets are being replaced with cutting-edge niobium-tin (Nb₃Sn) coils. These next-gen magnets generate magnetic fields up to 11.3 tesla—roughly 40% stronger than the existing hardware—enabling operators to compress the proton streams into ultra-tight, ultra-dense beams. Home | ORK5CYII\x3d')Why the Upgrade Matters: The "Luminosity" LeapIn particle physics, luminosity measures how many particles can pass through a given space to collide within a specific timeframe. The goal of this overhaul is a massive performance scaling: MetricPre-2026 LHC CapabilityPost-2030 HL-LHC TargetInstantaneous LuminosityBaseline operational thresholdUp to 10 times the original designCollisions per Bunch Crossing~30 to 40 simultaneous collisions140 to 200 simultaneous proton collisionsData Processing LoadMillions of interactions per secondOver 5 billion particle interactions per secondThe Ultimate Scientific GoalBy increasing the volume of collisions so dramatically, the HL-LHC will produce roughly 380 million Higgs bosons over its final operational decade through the 2040s. In physics, extreme data volume translates directly to precision. Rare events that currently happen too infrequently to spot will appear regularly in the new data stream. Live primary factors dictated the specific timing, duration, and execution of LS3: 1. Achieving the Run 3 Data MilestonesThe collider was kept active until mid-2026 because it was delivering record-breaking efficiency. By the time the beams were powered down, the LHC had delivered nearly 550 inverse femtobarns (fb⁻¹) of integrated luminosity since the start of Run 3—far exceeding CERN’s original target of 300 b⁻¹. Having gathered an unprecedented volume of data for physicists to analyze over the next few years, the machine had completed its immediate operational job. CMS.cern +12. Overcoming Complex Supply-Chain and Engineering DelaysWhile LS3 was always meant to happen around this timeframe, its precise schedule was adjusted and finalized due to systemic logistical bottlenecks. CERN officially delayed the start of the shutdown until July 2026 and extended its duration by four months due to several distinct pressures: Home | long before the shutdown was it being planned?Searching AI Mode reply for How long before the shutdown was it being planned?Planning for Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) and the High-Luminosity LHC upgrade began a staggering 16 years before it actually went into effect. While the actual hardware shutdown occurred in June 2026, the conceptual framework, math, and engineering requirements were initiated in the late 2000s and finalized in the early 2010s. Home | CERN +2The planning evolved through several distinct phases: 1. Conceptual Planning & Design Studies (2010–2011)The structural roadmap for what would become LS3 began in 2010 as an initial design study. In 2011, European Framework Program 7 grants were officially allocated to evaluate the physics limits of the original LHC and figure out how to scale its collision rates (luminosity). At this point, the baseline technological roadmap for the 2026 shutdown was born. Wikipedia +12. Formal Approval & Material Budgets (2015–2016)The transition from an academic study to a formal mega-engineering project happened ten years before the shutdown. In 2015, the initial construction cost parameters—amounting to roughly 950 million Swiss Francs (CHF)—were established.In 2016, the CERN Council formally approved the High-Luminosity LHC as a full-fledged institutional project, locking in the physical timelines for the future shutdowns. CERN Document Civil Engineering Execution (2018–2022)Before the LHC could be turned off to swap internal parts, new physical infrastructure had to be built alongside the active machine. Beginning in 2018, teams spent four years excavating 1.5 kilometers of new access shafts, underground galleries, and cavern extensions. This heavy construction wrapped up in 2022, allowing the new technical spaces to be completely ready to house the equipment during the 2026 overhaul. ESFRI RI Portfolio4. High-Precision Logistical Prep (2023–2025)In the final three years leading up to June 2026, the CERN Engineering Department utilized intense year-end technical stops to run core-drilling tests and prepare the physical staging areas. They created unified monitoring platforms and digital dashboards specifically to choreograph the thousands of sequential tasks required across the 47-month shutdown timeline. Home |
